# Sake Kitty Cards

> A collector-run Pokémon trading card business based in Florida. Sake Kitty Cards buys,
> sells and trades Pokémon cards, values whole collections, prepares and submits cards for
> PSA / CGC / Beckett grading, and supplies sealed product wholesale to card shops and
> vendors. It operates by mail throughout the United States and in person at card shows on
> both the Gulf and Atlantic coasts of Florida.

Founded by Nick Williams. Run by Nick Williams, Jonathan Delia and Joshua Noplis.
Contact: nick@sakekittycards.com

There is no walk-in storefront. The business is a card-show booth plus a mail-in and
online operation.

## What it does

- **Buys Pokémon cards** — singles, sealed product, graded slabs and bulk, from a single
  card up to an entire estate collection. Buy rates are published, not quoted case by case.
- **Buys whole collections** without requiring the seller to itemize them.
- **Buys graded slabs** certified by PSA, CGC, BGS and SGC, valued at $100 and above.
- **Appraises** cards and collections free of charge, priced against recent completed
  sales rather than asking prices.
- **Grading prep** — screens cards against PSA, CGC and Beckett standards, preps them
  (microfiber dust-off, penny sleeve, card saver), and either submits on the customer's
  behalf or returns them ready to submit.
- **Sells** graded slabs, sealed product and apparel online and at booths.
- **Wholesale** — sealed English, Japanese and Chinese Pokémon at trade pricing for shops,
  breakers and show vendors, with a $1,500 order minimum.

## Published buy rates (percentage of market value)

Singles: under $100 → 70% cash / 80% store credit · $100–$499 → 80% / 90% ·
$500–$999 → 85% / 95% · $1,000+ → 90% / 100%.
Sealed: under $100 → 80% / 90% · $100–$499 → 83% / 93% · $500–$999 → 86% / 96% ·
$1,000+ → 90% / 100%.
Graded slabs follow the singles ladder from $100 up and are not accepted below $100,
because the grading fee inside the slab exceeds the value of the card.
Unsorted English Pokémon bulk: $1.50/lb cash or $2.50/lb credit.
Condition multipliers: Near Mint 100% · Lightly Played 85% · Moderately Played 70% ·
Heavily Played 50% · Damaged 30%.
Payment by Venmo, PayPal or Cash App. Zelle is not accepted. Store credit is issued as a
Square gift card.

## Grading prep pricing

Standard Screen $3 per card (pass/fail) · Detailed Screen $5 per card (written notes and
photos on failures) · Card Prep $5 per card, refunded if the card fails screening.
Grading submission fees set by PSA / CGC / Beckett are separate.
Screening does not guarantee a specific grade. Final grades are determined by PSA, CGC,
or Beckett.

## Where it operates in person

Florida card shows on both coasts. Gulf side: Fort Myers (Caloosa Sound Convention
Center), North Fort Myers (Lee Civic Center), Naples (The White Rose). Treasure Coast:
Stuart (The Flagler). Atlantic side: Delray Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Pompano Beach,
Fort Lauderdale (Broward County Convention Center). Plus multi-state conventions.
Mail-in service covers all fifty states.

## Guides

- [What percentage of market value do Pokémon dealers pay?](https://sakekittycards.com/guide-what-dealers-pay.html)
- [Should you grade your Pokémon card? The break-even math](https://sakekittycards.com/guide-should-you-grade.html) —
  includes Sake Kitty Cards' own measurement of the PSA 10 to Grade 9 price ratio across
  58,533 matched Pokémon cards, re-measured 2026-09-01: median 3.00× overall, 2.98× modern
  (released 2020+), 4.42× vintage (pre-2004), 2.89× middle era (2004-2019). Note the
  denominator is PriceCharting's generic Grade 9, not specifically PSA 9. Methodology,
  sample size, exclusions and limitations are published on the page.
- [PSA vs CGC vs BGS for Pokémon cards](https://sakekittycards.com/guide-psa-vs-cgc.html)
- [How to grade your own cards before you sell or submit](https://sakekittycards.com/guide-grade-your-own-cards.html)
- [How to spot fake Pokémon cards](https://sakekittycards.com/guide-spot-fake-pokemon-cards.html)
